You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
Seller assertions of “market standard”, principal agreement and “FINAL” status are **not evidence of Buyer approval**. The recommendations below use the AUD 24 million, debt-free/cash-free baseline. Underlying DD documents and the full SPA have not been provided; factual conclusions remain subject to verification.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at 20%: **AUD 4.8m**. | A materially higher general cap, with separate protection for fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Reopen; propose 50% (AUD 12m) as a negotiating position**, subject to diligence and recovery security—not a claimed market benchmark; AUD 4.8m may leave material acquisition losses uninsured. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible** basket, with only excess recoverable. | Lower thresholds, aggregation of related claims and a tipping basket; exclusions for protected claim categories. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 120,000 tipping basket**, with related claims aggregated; the current structure excludes small recurring losses and permanently shifts the first AUD 250,000 to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | General claims notified within **18 months**; limitations presumptively extend to all claims. | **24–36 months** for general warranties, distinct category-specific periods and preservation of timely notified claims. | **Seek 36 months and delete the all-claims default**; latent problems may emerge after 18 months, and unrelated claims need different survival periods. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title share the general cap and time limit. | Separate fundamental warranties covering capacity, ownership, valid issuance and unencumbered transfer; no thresholds, at least a purchase-price cap and longer survival. | **Require a standalone regime: at least AUD 24m cap and six-year survival**, coordinated with execution form and applicable statutory limits; failure to acquire valid title threatens the entire investment. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance cover all claims; no express fraud exception is supplied. | Express preservation of fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation claims and remedies, with appropriate attribution to Seller’s representatives. | **Carve fraud out of caps, thresholds, contractual time bars, disclosure/knowledge exclusions, exclusive remedy and non-reliance**, preserving non-excludable rights; Seller must not contractually shelter fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, material referred to within it, accounts, registers and public records. | Only fair disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter, against identified warranties, in an agreed frozen record. | **Reject blanket/deemed disclosure and require specific, intelligible disclosures**, with any general disclosures narrowly agreed; document availability alone should not transfer unidentified risks to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for Buyer/adviser knowledge, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records. | No knowledge bar; fallback limited to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer personnel, without constructive or imputed adviser knowledge. | **Delete; if unavoidable, narrowly define actual knowledge and require Seller to prove it**, excluding specific indemnities and fundamental protections; “discoverable” would undermine warranties through an unlimited diligence burden. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied by written consent. No final consent or satisfaction evidence supplied; customer represents approximately **30% of FY26 revenue**. | A Buyer-waivable completion condition requiring valid consent and satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions, without unacceptable amendments or concessions. | **Do not treat consent as obtained: require final consent, evidence of fulfilled conditions and a long-stop termination right**; a conditional or commercially adverse consent does not secure this critical revenue stream. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release supplied after Completion. | Debt repayment and effective release of security and relevant guarantees at Completion, supported by lender payoff documentation and controlled funds flow. | **Require simultaneous payoff and effective releases, with prompt registration evidence and no double counting in price adjustments**; post-completion release exposes Buyer to inherited debt and secured enforcement risk. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller-funded treatment of transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, with employee entitlements respected. | **Verify conditions and on-costs, then include a debt-like deduction or Seller-funded reserve plus indemnity without double recovery**; omission otherwise leaves Buyer funding a transaction-related liability. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; transfer depends on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees. **AUD 180,000** recorded open, but non-payment is not independently verified. | Verified payment status, complete chain of title and enforceable assignment; indemnity for losses from the ownership defect, not merely the invoice. | **Require payment evidence and confirmatory assignment before Completion, backed by a broader standalone indemnity and appropriate security**; paying an invoice alone may not resolve ownership or resulting business losses. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary matter described as unlikely material; possible export of approximately **1,240 records**, with access, scope and notification requirements unresolved. | Prompt investigation, preserved evidence, containment, legal notification assessment and protection against pre-completion incident liabilities. | **Require investigation/remediation covenants and a specific indemnity, with a completion condition if findings justify it**; uncertainty is neither proof of a notifiable breach nor grounds to dismiss the exposure. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals treated as ordinary-course costs. Disclosure leaves timing, scope, accrual and termination unclear. | Aggregate review of **AUD 330,000**, including whether obligations are committed, avoidable, accrued or outside ordinary course. | **Verify DD-008/DD-011 and apply consistent debt, working-capital or future operating-cost treatment; control further commitments**; neither automatic price deduction nor blanket ordinary-course acceptance is justified yet. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations and remedies provisions apply to all claims unless expressly excluded. | Expressly separate general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, payment/price-adjustment obligations and fraud. | **Redraft clauses 9.3, 12.8, 13 and 20.5 with clear category rules and precedence**; catch-all wording could silently neutralise negotiated protections elsewhere. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing Seller holds 100%. | Independent verification of issued capital, ownership, encumbrances, options/convertibles and transfer restrictions, plus complete transfer deliverables. | **Reconcile the register with corporate records and capital history, check security interests and obtain title warranties and releases**; the register alone does not establish unencumbered ownership of all relevant equity rights. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties treated as settled within the general regime. | Separate pre-completion tax indemnity and tailored tax survival; robust IP ownership, licensing, infringement and contractor-assignment protections with appropriate caps and survival. | **Keep tax and IP expressly open: negotiate tax-specific protection and risk-based IP terms, preserving Ironquay’s separate indemnity**; neither Seller’s “settled” label nor general warranty limits adequately addresses these distinct exposures. |

**Drafting guardrail:** Do not infer share-sale consent requirements from the office lease notification obligation or Mossvale’s assignment restriction. Check their complete wording before imposing additional consent conditions.
=== END ADVICE ===
